title: Academic Verb Collocations

topic_snapshot.description: Essential verb-noun pairings that instantly elevate the academic tone of essays.

key_vocabulary_bank.example: The police have so far been unable to ascertain the cause of the explosion.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A detective looking intently through a magnifying glass at a clue, discovering the truth.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: To get or produce something, especially information or a reaction.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: The questionnaire was designed to elicit detailed feedback about the new product.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: An interviewer asking a profound question that brings out an emotional and thoughtful response from the interviewee.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: To suggest a theory, idea, or principle as a basic fact from which a further idea is formed.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: The linguist postulated that all human languages share a deep, underlying structure.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A scientist standing in front of a chalkboard filled with complex equations, presenting a new foundational theory.

collocation_builder.meaning: To carry out a systematic investigation.
collocation_builder.example: Universities conduct research to expand human knowledge.

collocation_builder.meaning: To start trying to solve a problem or worry.
collocation_builder.example: The government must urgently address the growing concern regarding air quality.

collocation_builder.meaning: To produce or provide findings or outcomes.
collocation_builder.example: The new teaching methodology is expected to yield positive results by the end of the semester.

upgrade_section.example: It is crucial to ascertain the root causes of urban poverty.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: Elicit a response / Provoke a reaction
upgrade_section.example: The controversial policy elicited a strong response from the public.
The internet makes it incredibly easy to disseminate information globally.

sentence_frames: To address this pressing concern, authorities must...
Recent studies conducted by experts yield results that suggest...
It is difficult to ascertain precisely why...

ielts_usage_examples.writing_example: Before implementing widespread educational reforms, it is vital to conduct comprehensive research to ascertain whether the new methods will yield tangible results.
ielts_usage_examples.speaking_example: If the council wants to address the concern of littering, they really need to disseminate information more effectively to elicit a change in public behavior.

common_mistakes: Using 'do research' instead of the stronger academic collocation 'conduct research' or 'carry out research'.
Writing 'make an effort to solve' when 'address an issue' is far more concise and academic.

quiz.question: Which verb accurately replaces 'get' in the phrase 'get a reaction from the crowd'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elicit' means to draw out a response, answer, or fact from someone in reaction to one's own actions or questions.

quiz.question: Which is the most natural academic collocation?
quiz.explanation: 'Conduct research' is the standard, most frequently used academic collocation in English.
